clue.text: Drivers get through distance that's unnatural

indicators.note: the drivers' club goes right through the middle of the distance word

parts.note: a mile is a distance
the RAC, Royal Automobile Club, is a British motoring organisation for drivers

explanation.surface: A complaint that motorists covering long distances is somehow against nature.
explanation.walkthrough: The RAC is the Royal Automobile Club, a British motorists' organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: A wonder is an event beyond the laws of nature, hence supernatural.

clue.text: Out of spite, start to malign girl

indicators.note: the start of the word malign is its first letter

parts.note: Alice is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Spitefully beginning to slander a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill will and spite are synonyms, the wish to harm.

parts.note: bring something back into someone's thoughts

explanation.surface: Persuade someone to reconsider.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Think again' suggests a change of mind; read literally it means call to mind once more.
explanation.definitionFit: To prompt a memory is to make a person think of something once more.

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go about, around, the match word
seed broadcast is scattered, so the letters of cannot are scattered

parts.note: a Test is an international cricket match

explanation.surface: A player who cannot be shown on TV around the game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' makes CONANT from cannot; 'about' puts it round TEST, a cricket Test match.
explanation.definitionFit: A person taking part in a contest is a competitor; direct synonym.

clue.text: Excellent performance on course for high-flyer

definitions.meaning: a golf score of two under par on a hole
a large bird of prey that soars high

explanation.surface: A star achiever's round on the golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: The bird soars high, and in golf the word names a score two under par.

parts.note: to make peace is to bury the axe-like tool of the idiom; until then there is no peace

explanation.surface: A grim remark that someone will find no rest until death.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a person's burial; the idiom 'bury the hatchet' means making peace.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: burying this small axe ends a quarrel, so until it is buried there is no peace.

clue.text: Fragment of Messiah heard, part of a cycle

indicators.note: heard tells us the spoken form of the phrase is what counts

parts.note: Messiah is by Handel, and a fragment of music is a bar

explanation.surface: A snippet of the oratorio Messiah on the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: A bar of Handel, composer of Messiah, said aloud matches the bicycle part.
explanation.definitionFit: The steering bar of a bicycle, a cycle, is part of it.

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words get a peep

explanation.surface: Take a quick look inside a ring binder.
explanation.definitionFit: Sticky tape binds things together, so it is a binder.

parts.note: the space above one's head, rather than high security clearance

explanation.surface: Security vetting of the highest grade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top-level clearance' suggests secret vetting; it is the space above your head.
explanation.definitionFit: The vertical space above a person or vehicle is clearance at head level.

clue.text: Assume control of Special K and overeat

indicators.note: special suggests a special version, so the letters are made into something different

explanation.surface: Bingeing on the breakfast cereal Special K.
explanation.walkthrough: Special K is a Kellogg's breakfast cereal.
explanation.definitionFit: To assume control of a company or task is to seize it; a phrasal synonym.

indicators.note: rotten fruit falls apart, so the letters of the word melon are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A melon has gone bad.
explanation.definitionFit: A citrus fruit, yellow and sour, a plain example of fruit.

clue.text: Board wanted to get you on board

definitions.text: Board wanted to get you on board

parts.words: Board wanted to get you on board
parts.note: the plank of wood you walk up to board a ship

explanation.surface: A company board seeks to recruit someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Board' first reads as directors; it is a wooden plank, and 'on board' means onto a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: This walkway is a plank laid from quay to deck so passengers can embark.

clue.text: Her husband-to-be was a slippery customer

definitions.text: Her husband-to-be was a slippery customer

parts.words: Her husband-to-be was a slippery customer
parts.note: the prince in the fairy tale identified his bride by a glass slipper

explanation.surface: A woman's fiancé was untrustworthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slippery customer' means a rogue, but here it is the prince who tried the glass slipper on everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: In the fairy tale, the prince searching with the glass slipper is the heroine's future husband.

clue.text: Trunk not to be opened roughly

indicators.note: a word that is not opened loses its first letter

parts.note: the trunk of the body is the torso

explanation.surface: An instruction on a storage trunk that it must stay shut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not to be opened' removes the T from the start of TORSO.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means approximately, as in 'ten or so', an everyday synonym.

definitions.meaning: to be dismissed from a job
literally, to have the blade come down on the neck

explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for losing one's job, also read literally as being beheaded.

indicators.note: a rioting crowd is in disorder, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A determined crowd on the rampage is causing annoyance.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean causing annoyance or difficulty; a direct synonym.

clue.text: Less popular time to be on shore, presumably, with boy

parts.note: on shore one is off the sea
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A quieter holiday period at the seaside with a lad.
explanation.definitionFit: The quiet months for tourism, when fewer people visit.

parts.note: players of music form a band
got on in years means aged

explanation.surface: The musicians took the stage drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plastered' reads as drunk, but means covered with sticking plaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Plastered here means covered in sticking plasters, i.e. dressed.

clue.text: Musical would be fine, if shortened

definitions.text: Musical would be fine, if shortened

parts.words: Musical would be fine, if shortened
parts.note: the state's postal abbreviation is OK, which means fine

explanation.surface: A long stage show would be all right if cut.
explanation.walkthrough: The Rodgers and Hammerstein show is named after a US state abbreviated OK.
explanation.definitionFit: A Rodgers and Hammerstein stage musical whose title shortens to a word for fine.

clue.text: Seeking computer technology is inviting trouble

parts.note: seeking something is ...
IT is information technology

explanation.surface: Wanting computer tech is a recipe for problems.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: behaving in a way that provokes a bad outcome, deserving what comes.

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
sago is a starchy grain used like a cereal

explanation.surface: Someone making a real effort with a breakfast bowl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tries hard' looks like the definition; the def is just 'Tries', with H from 'hard'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means makes an attempt, an idiom for trying.

indicators.note: something done appallingly is done badly, so the letters are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Was someone held back? Their cheating is shocking.
explanation.definitionFit: Pure or modest, restrained in sexual conduct; the question mark flags a looser synonym.

clue.text: Precious way to start a letter

definitions.meaning: the usual salutation opening a letter, as in 'Sir' preceded by it

explanation.definitionFit: The word means beloved and also opens a letter's salutation.

definitions.meaning: a coating of render with small stones, applied to the walls of a house
a small stone's quick rush, read whimsically

explanation.walkthrough: 'Housecoat' looks like a dressing gown; it is a coat for a house. A pebble's dash is literally a small stone's throw.
explanation.definitionFit: This rough render studded with gravel is a coating for exterior house walls.

clue.text: A block picked up is wood

indicators.note: in a down clue, picked up means lifted, so the letters read upwards

parts.note: a slab is a block

explanation.surface: Lifting a block of timber.
explanation.definitionFit: A very light tropical timber used for models, so a kind of wood.

explanation.surface: A quick trim that was cheap.
explanation.definitionFit: A small scissor cut, and British slang for something cheap.

parts.note: crushed coffee is ground

indicators.note: oddly takes the first, third and fifth letters of the word smells

explanation.surface: A weed that has been crushed gives off a strange smell.
explanation.definitionFit: A common garden weed with small yellow flowers, an example of the class.

parts.note: senior teachers running schools, and the call made when a coin is tossed

explanation.surface: A teacher picks pupils at random.
explanation.walkthrough: The coin-toss call is chosen at random; head teachers are the senior teachers.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names head teachers and is also a call made on a coin toss.

clue.text: Showing no emotion over divine corpse

indicators.note: the corpse word is placed over, that is ahead of, the divine one

parts.note: a corpse is dead
Pan is a Greek god, a divine being

explanation.surface: A stony face over the body of a god.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes an expressionless face or delivery, especially in humour.

parts.note: an app is a function on a smartphone
to roam is to rove

explanation.surface: Praising a phone feature that lets you use it abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean to express a favourable view of something; close synonyms.
